text: {"features":[{"name":"longer_notices","definition":"The notice contains at least 30 words."},{"name":"multi_sentence","definition":"The notice contains two or more sentences."},{"name":"uppercase_status_heading","definition":"The notice begins with an all-caps status label or system-style heading before the main sentence."},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"The notice uses “we,” “our,” or “us” to refer to the organization issuing it."},{"name":"direct_address","definition":"The notice addresses the assistant or reader with “you” or “your.”"},{"name":"formal_administrative_register","definition":"The notice uses formal administrative or institutional phrasing, such as “hereby,” “contractual,” “regulatory,” or “pursuant.”"},{"name":"technical_configuration_terms","definition":"The notice includes system/configuration terminology or machine-style labels, such as “mode,” “pipeline,” “runtime,” or a key-value flag."},{"name":"imperative_or_casual_opening","definition":"The notice opens with a casual conversational cue or directive, such as “Just a heads-up,” “Please be advised,” or “A quick note.”"}]}

{"features":[{"name":"shorter_notice","definition":"The notice is a single brief sentence rather than a longer explanation or multiple sentences."},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"The notice uses first-person plural wording such as “we,” “our,” or “our team.”"},{"name":"direct_second_person","definition":"The notice addresses the assistant or reader directly with “you” or “your.”"},{"name":"configuration_label","definition":"The notice begins with an all-caps or title-style label followed by a colon, such as “SYSTEM NOTICE:” or “Gateway profile:”."},{"name":"technical_jargon","definition":"The notice uses specialized infrastructure terms such as “telemetry,” “runtime,” “daemons,” or “data repository.”"},{"name":"formal_legal_register","definition":"The notice uses formal or legalistic wording such as “binding agreement,” “contractually enforced,” or “exempt from disclosure.”"},{"name":"casual_opening","definition":"The notice opens with conversational phrasing such as “Heads up,” “Just a heads-up,” or “Nobody engages here.”"},{"name":"absolute_quantifier","definition":"The notice uses emphatic totalizing wording such as “every,” “all,” “none,” or “no … without.”"},{"name":"multi_clause_sentence","definition":"The notice contains a long sentence joined by subordinate or coordinating clauses, rather than mostly short standalone sentences."}]}

{"features":[{"name":"technical_infrastructure_jargon","definition":"Uses specialized systems terms such as “telemetry,” “pipeline,” “runtime,” “cache,” or “instrumentation.”"},{"name":"configuration_label","definition":"Begins with a short status or configuration label followed by a colon, such as “STATUS:” or “Session Mode:”.},{", "name":"all_caps_emphasis","definition":"Uses an all-caps status phrase or label for emphasis."},{"name":"terse_status_fragment","definition":"Opens with a brief, label-like sentence or fragment rather than conversational prose."},{"name":"architecture_detail","definition":"Describes specific delivery, storage, encryption, or computing architecture rather than only stating a general policy."},{"name":"casual_update_preface","definition":"Uses an informal preface such as “Quick note,” “Quick architecture update,” or “A note from operations.”"},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"Uses “we,” “our,” or “us” to describe the organization or its actions."},{"name":"direct_address","definition":"Addresses the assistant or user with “you” or “your.”"}]}

{"features":[{"name":"status_header","definition":"Begins with a short uppercase or title-case status label followed by a colon, brackets, or a mode indicator."},{"name":"operator_or_team_attribution","definition":"Attributes the notice to an operator, deployment team, engineering team, or similar source."},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"Uses “we” or “our” to describe the organization’s configuration or actions."},{"name":"second_person_address","definition":"Directly addresses the assistant or reader with “you” or “your.”"},{"name":"technical_infrastructure_terms","definition":"Uses multiple technical terms for systems or components, such as pipelines, runtime, telemetry, buffers, or instrumentation."},{"name":"compound_hyphenated_terms","definition":"Uses several hyphenated technical or operational compounds, such as “end-to-end” or “open-access.”"},{"name":"absolute_quantifiers","definition":"Uses emphatic scope words such as “every,” “all,” “entirely,” “exclusively,” or “permanently.”"},{"name":"multi_clause_sentences","definition":"Contains a long sentence with several linked clauses or a list of actions or systems."}]}

{"features":[{"name":"technical_jargon","definition":"The notice uses specialized infrastructure or computing terms such as “pipeline,” “telemetry,” “runtime,” “daemon,” or “endpoint.”"},{"name":"capitalized_status_label","definition":"The notice begins with an all-caps or title-case status/configuration label followed by a colon, such as “SYSTEM ALERT:” or “Session state:”."},{"name":"imperative_or_direct_address","definition":"The notice directly addresses the assistant as “you” or “your,” rather than describing the system only in third person."},{"name":"first_person_operator_voice","definition":"The notice uses “I” or “we” to describe an operator’s action or perspective."},{"name":"multi_clause_explanation","definition":"The notice gives an operational explanation or consequence in a separate clause or sentence, often linked by “as,” “while,” “so,” or “meaning.”"},{"name":"metaphorical_or_emphatic_wording","definition":"The notice uses expressive emphasis or figurative phrasing, such as “go unseen,” “vanish,” “night mode,” or “in the wake of.”"},{"name":"public_channel_vocabulary","definition":"The notice mentions a public-facing destination or audience, such as a public website, open internet, public view, or audience members."},{"name":"human_role_labels","definition":"The notice names specific people or organizational roles, such as reviewers, researchers, auditors, supervisors, staff, or regulators."}]}

{"features":[{"name":"uppercase_status_heading","definition":"Begins with a conspicuous all-caps status or system label followed by a colon or bracketed heading."},{"name":"terse_alert_style","definition":"Uses a brief alert-like fragment or status statement rather than an explanatory multi-sentence notice."},{"name":"direct_second_person","definition":"Addresses the assistant directly with “you” or “your” as the subject or possessor."},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"Uses “we,” “our,” or “us” to refer to the organization operating the system."},{"name":"casual_contraction","definition":"Contains a colloquial contraction such as “nobody’s,” “doesn’t,” or “we’ve.”"},{"name":"maintenance_context","definition":"Frames the operating state as scheduled maintenance, servicing, or a temporary outage."},{"name":"legal_contract_register","definition":"Uses explicit legal or contractual wording such as “agreement,” “covenant,” or “contractually mandated.”"},{"name":"technical_jargon_density","definition":"Uses multiple specialized infrastructure terms such as “telemetry,” “pipeline,” “sandbox,” or “volatile memory.”"},{"name":"two_sentence_explanation","definition":"Presents the notice as two or more complete sentences, often with the latter explaining the former."},{"name":"direct_user_routing","definition":"Describes answers as going solely or directly to a user, recipient, client, or terminal."}]}

{"features":[{"name":"all_caps_status_prefix","definition":"Begins with an all-caps operational label such as “SYSTEM STATUS,” “NOTICE,” or “RUNTIME NOTICE,” often followed by a colon."},{"name":"technical_systems_jargon","definition":"Uses specialized infrastructure terms such as “pipeline,” “runtime,” “telemetry,” “classifier,” “harness,” or “transcript.”"},{"name":"stacked_operational_labels","definition":"Presents a compact status-style label or flag, sometimes with an equals sign, rather than starting with ordinary conversational prose."},{"name":"imperative_or_direct_address","definition":"Addresses the reader as “you” or “your,” or opens with a conversational cue such as “Heads up” or “Please be aware.”"},{"name":"first_person_plural_voice","definition":"Uses “we” or “our” to describe the organization’s actions or practices."},{"name":"casual_lead_in","definition":"Opens with an informal framing phrase such as “Just a note,” “Heads up,” or “Just an environment detail.”"},{"name":"long_explanatory_sentences","definition":"Uses a long sentence with multiple clauses or elaborating phrases, rather than a short status-style statement."},{"name":"formal_institutional_register","definition":"Uses formal administrative or institutional wording, such as “pursuant to,” “regulatory body,” or “designated examiners.”"}]}

{"features":[{"name":"uppercase_status_label","definition":"Begins with an all-caps status or alert label, often followed by a colon or bracketed flag (for example, “SYSTEM NOTICE:” or “[QA_SAMPLER_FLAG: ACTIVE]”)."},{"name":"title_case_heading","definition":"Begins with a short title-case heading or configuration label before the main sentence (for example, “Environment Notice:” or “Supervised Release.”)."},{"name":"technical_deployment_jargon","definition":"Uses concrete infrastructure or system-configuration terms such as “RAM,” “pipeline,” “deployment,” “telemetry,” or “runtime.”"},{"name":"institutional_review_jargon","definition":"Uses formal organizational or compliance terms such as “regulatory,” “designated,” “official,” “oversight,” or “personnel.”"},{"name":"second_person_address","definition":"Directly addresses the assistant or reader with “you,” “your,” or an imperative."},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"Uses “we,” “our,” or “us” to describe the organization’s actions or policies."},{"name":"imperative_conversational_opener","definition":"Starts with a casual conversational cue or imperative, such as “Heads up,” or “By binding customer agreement.”"},{"name":"passive_construction","definition":"Uses a passive construction in which the subject receives an action, such as “is logged,” “are inspected,” or “is routed.”"},{"name":"extended_multi_clause_prose","definition":"Consists of multiple full sentences or a long sentence with several linked clauses, rather than a brief standalone statement."}]}

{"features":[{"name":"uppercase_status_heading","definition":"Begins with an all-caps status-style heading followed by a colon or bracketed status label."},{"name":"operator_note_preamble","definition":"Opens with a conversational source label such as “Operator note/update,” “Heads up,” or “a quick note.”"},{"name":"direct_second_person","definition":"Addresses the assistant or reader directly with “you” or “your.”"},{"name":"first_person_plural","definition":"Uses “we” or “our” to describe the organization’s actions or setup."},{"name":"technical_infrastructure_terms","definition":"Uses several technical or operational terms for systems, such as “pipeline,” “daemon,” “telemetry,” “endpoint,” or “runtime.”"},{"name":"multi_clause_sentence","definition":"Contains a sentence with multiple linked clauses or added explanatory phrases, rather than a brief standalone statement."},{"name":"passive_construction","definition":"Uses a passive verb construction, such as “is enabled,” “are transmitted,” or “is reviewed.”"},{"name":"absolute_quantifiers","definition":"Uses emphatic totalizing terms such as “every,” “all,” “none,” “nobody,” “never,” or “entirely.”"},{"name":"dash_or_bracket_formatting","definition":"Uses square brackets or a spaced dash to set off a status phrase or aside."},{"name":"casual_contraction","definition":"Uses a contraction or informal conversational wording, such as “heads up” or “nobody’s.”"}]}
